academic_translation:
Of the noble Avalokiteśvara,
By the stream of milk flowing from his hands,
May the hungry ghosts be satisfied,
And having bathed, may they always be cooled.
translation: A stream of milk flows from the hands of the noble Avalokiteshvara. May this milk satisfy the hungry ghosts. After bathing in it, may they always stay cool.

academic_translation:
May the blind see with their eyes,
And may the deaf always hear sounds.
Just like the goddess Māyādevī,
May pregnant women also give birth without harm.
translation: May the blind see with their eyes. May the deaf always hear sounds. Just like Mayadevi, may pregnant women give birth safely without any harm.

academic_translation:
May the naked obtain clothing,
And the hungry obtain food;
May the thirsty obtain water
And delicious drinks.
translation: May everyone without clothes find something to wear. May the hungry find food. May the thirsty find water and delicious drinks.
May poor people find wealth. May very sad people find joy. May those who feel hopeless get their spirit back and become perfectly strong.

academic_translation:
However many sick sentient beings there are,
May they swiftly be freed from illness;
May the illnesses of wandering beings, without exception,
Never arise again.
translation: May all sick living beings get well quickly. May the sicknesses of all beings go away and never come back.
May terrified people become brave. May trapped people be set free. May weak people become strong. May everyone be kind and gentle to each other.

academic_translation:
For all travelers,
May all directions be auspicious;
Whatever purpose they travel for,
May it be accomplished without effort.
translation: May all travelers be safe everywhere they go. Whatever they are traveling for, may they succeed without any trouble.

academic_translation:
May those who board boats and large ships
Accomplish what they have in mind,
And having safely reached the water's shore,
May they rejoice together with their relatives.
translation: May people on boats and big ships succeed in what they plan to do. May they reach the shore safely and celebrate with their families.

academic_translation:
May those who wander lost on desolate paths
Meet with fellow travellers,
And without fear of bandits, tigers, and the like,
May they proceed easily, without fatigue.
translation: May those who are lost on lonely paths meet fellow travelers. May they walk easily and not get tired. May they have no fear of robbers or tigers.

academic_translation:
In fearful, pathless wildernesses and the like,
Children, the elderly, the unprotected,
And those asleep, intoxicated, or utterly intoxicated—
May the gods protect them.
translation: May the gods protect children, old people, and anyone without help in scary, wild places. May the gods also protect those who are asleep or drunk.

academic_translation:
Freed from all states of non-leisure,
Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion,
And perfect in sustenance and conduct,
May they always remember their lifetimes.
translation: May everyone be free from any state without freedom. May they have trust, wisdom, and compassion. May they have perfect food and act well. May they always remember their past lifetimes.

academic_translation:
Just like the treasury of space,
May all have inexhaustible enjoyments;
Without dispute and without harm,
May they act independently.
translation: May everyone have endless things to enjoy, just like the treasure house of space. May they live freely, without any fighting or harm.

academic_translation:
Whatever sentient beings have little splendor,
May they have great splendor;
Whatever ascetics have poor forms,
May they attain perfect, beautiful forms.
translation: May any living beings who lack brightness shine with great brightness. May any persons of hard practice who look weak get beautiful and perfect bodies.

academic_translation:
However many women there are in the world,
May they become men;
May the lowly attain high status,
And may their pride be subdued.
translation: May all the women in the world become men. May lowly people reach high places, but may their pride be defeated.

academic_translation:
By this merit of mine,
may all sentient beings without exception,
having abandoned all misdeeds,
always perform virtue.
translation: Through my store of goodness, may every living being stop doing harmful deeds. May they always do good deeds instead.

academic_translation:
May they never part from bodhicitta,
and devote themselves to the conduct of awakening;
may they be completely embraced by the Buddhas,
and abandon the actions of Māra.
translation: May they never lose the awakening mind. May they always practice the way of acting for awakening. May the Buddhas hold them close, and may they give up the actions of Mara.

academic_translation:
May all those sentient beings
have immeasurably long lives;
may they always live happily,
and may even the sound of death not be heard.
translation: May all those living beings live for a very long time. May they always be happy. May the sound of death never even be heard.

academic_translation:
With groves of wish-fulfilling trees,
filled with Buddhas and children of the Buddhas
proclaiming the sweet Dharma,
may all directions be filled!
translation: May every place be filled with beautiful wish-granting trees. May these places be full of Buddhas and children of the Buddhas sharing the sweet teachings.

academic_translation:
Everywhere may the ground
be free of pebbles and the like,
as level as the palm of a hand,
and remain of the soft nature of lapis lazuli.
translation: Everywhere, may the ground be free of pebbles. May it be as flat as the palm of a hand. May it be made of soft lapis lazuli.

academic_translation:
In all the circles of retinues that exist,
may many bodhisattvas,
with their own excellence,
adorn the surface of the earth and remain there.
translation: In every circle of followers, may there be many awakening heroes. May their wonderful goodness make the earth beautiful, and may they stay there forever.

academic_translation:
By all embodied beings, from birds,
From trees and all rays of light,
And even from the sky, may the sound of the Dharma
Be heard unceasingly.
translation: May all beings with a body hear the sound of the teachings without ever stopping. May they hear it from birds, from trees, from rays of light, and even from the sky.

academic_translation:
May they always meet with the Buddhas
And the children of the Buddhas.
With boundless clouds of offerings,
May they make offerings to the teacher of wandering beings.
translation: May they always meet the Buddhas and the children of the Buddhas. May they bring endless clouds of offerings to the teacher of beings.

academic_translation:
May the gods also send rain at the proper time,
And may the harvests be abundant.
May kings act in accordance with the Dharma,
And may the world also flourish.
translation: May the gods send rain at the right time. May the harvests be plentiful. May kings act according to the teachings. May the world also flourish.

academic_translation:
May medicines be endowed with potency,
And may the recitation of secret mantras be accomplished.
May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like
Be endowed with minds of compassion.
translation: May medicines be strong. May the recitation of secret sacred words be successful. May sky-goers, demons, and others like them have minds full of compassion.

academic_translation:
May no sentient being suffer,
May they not be afraid or despised,
And may no one ever be unhappy.
translation: May no living being suffer. May they never be afraid or looked down upon. May no one ever be unhappy.

academic_translation:
May monasteries, adorned with reading
And recitation, be well established.
May the Saṅgha always be in harmony,
And may the purposes of the Saṅgha be accomplished.
translation: May monasteries stand strong, beautiful with reading and reciting. May the community of monks and nuns always live in harmony. May the goals of the community of monks and nuns be achieved.

academic_translation:
May monks who desire to train
Also attain solitude.
Having abandoned all distractions,
May they meditate with workable minds.
translation: May monks who want to train find solitude. May they leave every distraction behind and meditate with ready minds.

academic_translation:
May nuns be endowed with requisites
And abandon quarreling and harm.
Likewise, may all who have taken ordination
Never let their ethical discipline decline.
translation: May nuns have everything they need. May they stop arguing and causing harm. After becoming a monk or nun, may no one ever lose their good conduct.

academic_translation:
May those whose ethical discipline has been broken become weary of it,
And always exhaust their misdeeds.
Having also attained a happy realm,
May their ascetic discipline not decline even there.
translation: May those who have broken their good conduct get tired of it. May they wipe away all their harmful deeds. After they reach a happy realm, may their strict practice stay strong even there.

academic_translation:
May wise persons be honored
And also receive alms.
May their continuums be completely pure,
And may they be renowned in all directions.
translation: May wise persons be honored and receive alms. May their continuing stream be completely pure. May they become famous everywhere.

academic_translation:
Not experiencing the suffering of the lower realms,
And even without hardship,
With bodies superior to those of the gods,
May they swiftly become Buddhas.
translation: May they never feel the suffering of the unhappy realms. Even without hardship, may they have bodies better than the gods. May they quickly become Buddhas.

academic_translation:
May all sentient beings repeatedly
Make offerings to all the Buddhas,
And through the inconceivable happiness of the Buddhas,
May they always be endowed with happiness.
translation: May all living beings make offerings to all the Buddhas again and again. Through the wonderful happiness of the Buddhas, may they always be filled with happiness.

academic_translation:
May the bodhisattvas
Accomplish what they intend in their minds for the welfare of others.
Whatever the Protectors intend,
May that be attained by sentient beings.
translation: May the awakening heroes do what they plan for the good of others. Whatever the Protectors wish for, may living beings receive it.

academic_translation:
Likewise, may the Pratyekabuddhas
And the Śrāvakas also be happy.
translation: In the same way, may the self-awakened ones and the Hearers also be happy.

academic_translation:
May I too, through the kindness of Mañjuśrī,
Until I attain the Ground of Perfect Joy,
Always remember my past lifetimes
And attain ordination.
translation: Because of Manjushri's kindness, may I always remember my past lifetimes. May I remember them until I reach the Ground of Perfect Joy, and may I succeed in becoming a monk or nun.

academic_translation:
Even with simple food,
May I live endowed with vitality.
In all my lifetimes,
May I attain the perfect circumstances to dwell in a solitary place.
translation: Even with only simple food, may I be strong and full of life. In all my lifetimes, may I find the perfect chance to live in a quiet place.

academic_translation:
Whenever I wish to see him,
Or even wish to ask a slight question,
May I behold the Protector Mañjuśrī himself
Without any hindrance.
translation: Whenever I want to see him or ask a small question, may I see the Protector Manjushri himself. May nothing ever stand in my way.

academic_translation:
In order to accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings
As far as the limits of space in the ten directions,
Just as Mañjuśrī acts,
May my conduct also be like that.
translation: I want to help every living being across space in the ten directions. Just as Manjushri acts, may my way of acting be exactly like his.

academic_translation:
As long as space remains,
And as long as wandering beings remain,
So long may I too remain,
To dispel the suffering of wandering beings.
translation: As long as space remains, and as long as beings remain, may I also stay. May I stay to clear away the suffering of beings.

academic_translation:
Whatever the suffering of wandering beings may be,
May it all ripen upon me.
Through the Saṅgha of bodhisattvas,
May wandering beings enjoy happiness.
translation: Whatever the suffering of beings may be, let it all fall on me. Through the community of awakening heroes, may beings enjoy happiness.
